findings.title: F-6 P0-DBA-01 trigger migration applied, but no test exercises the raw-query bypass path the trigger is designed to block — the absence-of-defense test is missing
findings.evidence_read: StockMovementsAppendOnlyTest:15-45 tests $movement->update() and $movement->delete() — these go through StockMovement::booted() updating()/deleting() callbacks which throw \LogicException. Both tests would pass even if the migration 2026_05_18_140000 were rolled back (i.e. triggers removed). The trigger migration's RAISE(ABORT) is verified ONLY by migration file presence + migrate:status='Ran'.
findings.impact: If a future refactor accidentally drops the Eloquent boot guards (e.g. extracting a trait, replacing Model with a generic table abstraction), AND if a contributor mistakenly thinks the triggers cover all paths, the regression escapes both unit tests AND code review. The Foundation F-6 P0-DBA-01 narrative claims defense-in-depth — the test surface should validate BOTH layers independently.
findings.recommendation: Add 2 new test methods to StockMovementsAppendOnlyTest: (a) test_raw_delete_blocked_by_db_trigger() — invokes DB::table('stock_movements')->where('id', $id)->delete() and asserts QueryException (SQLite: 'stock_movements is append-only' RAISE; MySQL: SQLSTATE 45000). (b) test_raw_update_blocked_by_db_trigger() — same pattern with ->update(['delta' => -99]). Both paths bypass Eloquent and exercise the trigger directly.
findings.scope_minimal_fix: HEAL-NOW eligible if added to a clean test file (not frozen). 2 test methods, ~20 lines total. Defer if WF-7 RED-META prefers a separate trigger-coverage sentinel test file.

findings.title: stock_levels non-negative on_hand guard is Eloquent-layer only — no DB CHECK constraint
findings.evidence_read: StockLevel:66-74 — saving() callback throws InvalidArgumentException for on_hand<0, reserved<0, reserved>on_hand. Migration 2026_04_27_143120_create_stock_levels_table.php — no CHECK constraint on these columns.
findings.actual_behavior: DB::table('stock_levels')->update(['on_hand' => -1]) succeeds at DB level. Eloquent boot guards bypassed. The append-only triggers protect stock_movements raw-query path (F-6 P0-DBA-01 fix) but stock_levels remains soft. Composite real-world exploit: an admin migration script could lower on_hand via raw query.
findings.impact: LOW V1 (no production raw stock_levels writes — all paths through StockService::mutateForOrderInTransaction or AvailabilityService::toggleStockable use Eloquent). MID V2 if SaaS multi-tenant bulk-update admin tooling is introduced.
findings.recommendation: Defer V1.0.2 — add CHECK (on_hand >= 0) AND CHECK (reserved >= 0) AND CHECK (reserved <= on_hand) via separate migration. MySQL >= 8.0.16 enforces, SQLite enforces. Old MariaDB <10.2.1 parses-but-ignores so document the floor.

findings.title: stock_movements.reason enum drift risk — migration locks 6 values but no code-level validator
findings.evidence_read: Migration L16 — enum('reason', ['order_created', 'order_canceled', 'refund', 'manual_in', 'manual_out', 'rupture_set']). StockService writes 'order_created' (:29) + 'order_canceled' / 'refund' (:37). No code path emits 'manual_in', 'manual_out', or 'rupture_set' — those are forward-compat reserved values.
findings.actual_behavior: Mixing string-typing approach. Adding a 7th reason would require a migration + enum alteration (MySQL ALTER TABLE rebuilds the column). Code-side, there's no PHP-enum-backed type for $reason — typos like 'order_canceled' vs 'order_cancelled' would silently insert a row that fails MySQL ENUM strict check.
findings.impact: LOW — DB-level enum check catches typos at INSERT time. Migration overhead per new reason is unique-but-not-blocking.
findings.recommendation: Defer V1.0.2 — promote $reason to a backed PHP enum (App\Enums\Stock\MovementReason) so callsites are compile-time safe. Concurrent migration to widen enum is the same effort either way.

findings.title: stock_movements.idempotency_key is nullable() but the listener flow always writes a key — nullable allows historical/manual rows without uniqueness
findings.evidence_read: Migration L19 — $table->string('idempotency_key')->nullable()->unique(). UNIQUE on nullable column — DB treats multiple NULLs as non-conflicting (PostgreSQL standard; MySQL also allows multiple NULLs on UNIQUE index). StockService::movementKey() always generates a non-null key (StockService:343), so V1 production rows always have a key. The nullable() is a forward-compat affordance for V1.1 manual stock adjustments where admin might insert untracked corrections.
findings.impact: LOW — V1 nominal path keys every row. The future manual_in / manual_out reason would need to opt into a key (e.g. 'manual:branch:user:timestamp:rand') for traceability.
findings.recommendation: When manual_in/manual_out admin UI ships in V1.1, REQUIRE non-null idempotency_key at controller layer (FormRequest validation) and consider making the column NOT NULL via migration after the surface is live.
